Let me analyze this conflict.

Register: "Tüm Elektronik Mühendislik San. Ve Tic. Ltd.Sti."
Document: "TÜM ELEKTRONİK MÜHENDİSLİK SAN. TİC. LTD. ŞTİ"

Differences:
- Case: register is mixed case, document is all caps (with Turkish dotted İ). Case difference = spelling drift, same-entity.
- Accents: "Tüm" vs "TÜM", "Mühendislik" vs "MÜHENDİSLİK" — Turkish uppercase. Same.
- "San. Ve Tic. Ltd.Sti." vs "SAN. TİC. LTD. ŞTİ" — "Ve" dropped in document; "Ltd.Sti." vs "LTD. ŞTİ" — same suffix, different transliteration ("sti" vs "ŞTİ" — Turkish uppercase of "şti"). Legal-suffix drift. Same-entity.

So verdict: same-entity. Best value: which one? The rule says same-entity — the rules don't explicitly say which value to take for same-entity. For number/year format differences, register's canonical form. For applicant same-entity, presumably pick the better-formed value. The register value "Tüm Elektronik Mühendislik San. Ve Tic. Ltd.Sti." includes "Ve" (and). The document omits "Ve". Both are fine; register seems canonical. Also the document is all-caps which is typical of certificate formatting; the register form is more normalized. I'd pick the register's value as best_value, noting same-entity.

Actually the rules: same-entity verdict — for spelling drift etc., no explicit best_value rule, but reasonable to pick the register's canonical form (register is the OIML-CS database). The document is the legal instrument though... but for same-entity name normalization, register's mixed-case form is cleaner. I'll go with register value.

One sentence why: "Same company; differences are case, Turkish accent, and legal-suffix formatting only."
